status: built 2026-10-08 (tools/tm_gate.py, pack cobblers_tm_gate, world-local); the badge rule switched to the power rule 2026-10-08; the owner's four calls of 2026-10-08 applied (groups 3, 9, 16 and badge_rule.chain), and Spore lowered to 5 for Stun Spore (group 18); NOT run in game: experiments/EXP-067-tm-recipe-gate
decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'Gate the recipes by badge.' Each crafted TM unlocks at the same badge as its shelf line: crafting stays the cheap route, but no earlier than the shelf (docs/research/DROP_RATE_CONSUMERS.md 3.3: with alpha gems 16 of the 23 income-gated shelf TMs were craftable before their shelf price was affordable). Every other TM unlocks by what its move does: the power rule, badge_rule.decision

mechanism.rung: configuration + datapack + functions (CLAUDE.md principle 6): the vanilla gamerule doLimitedCrafting, the vanilla recipe book, recipe advancements and /recipe. No mod, no scripting layer
mechanism.why_not_cheaper: Cobblemon native: no per-player recipe hook (TMCraft TMs are vanilla crafting_shapeless / crafting_shaped recipes, read from tmcraft-1.4.19+1.8.0.jar data/tmcraft/recipe/). Addon: TMCraft has no crafting hook or config (its only gamerule is consumeMoveItemOnUse, kiwiapollo/tmcraft/gamerule/ModGameRule.class). Fabric resource conditions (the Beast Ball's rung) act at load, server-wide, and cannot read a player
mechanism.verified_from_jar: Minecraft 1.21.1 (client jar 1.21.1-0.19.5, official names, intermediary-1.21.1 for the mapping), read 2026-10-08: RecipeCraftingHolder (crk / class_1732) default setRecipeUsed(Level, ServerPlayer, RecipeHolder) (method_7665) allows a recipe when recipe.isSpecial() || !gamerules.getBoolean(doLimitedCrafting) || player.getRecipeBook().contains(recipe). Its ONLY caller in the jar is CraftingMenu.slotChangedCraftingGrid (cqm / class_1714 method_17399), used by the crafting table and the inventory's 2x2 grid. Furnaces, smithing, the stonecutter and the Crafter block do not call it. doLimitedCrafting defaults to false (GameRules dcs.w, iconst_0)
mechanism.what_it_does_to_every_other_recipe: under doLimitedCrafting a grid recipe a player has not unlocked cannot be crafted at all. So the pack never relies on each recipe's own unlock: on a player's first tick under a new plan, tm_gate/sync runs `recipe give @s *` (every recipe the server loaded, vanilla, Cobblemon and every mod) and then takes back only the gated recipes of the badges that player does not hold. Nothing is stranded for anyone; the sweep (`python tools/tm_gate.py sweep`) counts what WOULD be stranded without that give
mechanism.sync_key: the plan's hash (every loaded recipe id and every gated recipe with its badge) is the score cobblers.tmgate a synced player carries: a new mod, a changed badge or a new TM recipe changes the hash at the next prepare, and every player re-syncs on their next tick
mechanism.earning: one advancement per badge, cobblers:tm_gate/earn/<flag>, minecraft:tick with the player holding cobblers:flag/<flag> (tools/progression_pack.py), rewards the function tm_gate/give/<flag>: `recipe give` of that badge's gated recipes. A sync revokes it for every badge the player lacks, so a revoked flag re-earns
mechanism.unlock_advancements: every loaded advancement whose rewards.recipes names a gated recipe (TMCraft's recipes/misc/tm_*, vanilla's and Carved Wood's crafter unlocks, Tom's crafting terminal's) is written back at its own path closed (fabric:load_conditions that never pass, the tools/key_ball.py form), else holding an ingredient would unlock the recipe early

gated.why: every TMCraft TM recipe the server loads is one of these two types (805 of them, read from the jar and COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31's added recipes). The 929 to_cobblemon_tm_* conversions (a TMCraft TM into a Cobblemon TM of the same move) are not gated: they need the TM already. The smelting recipes into legacy_* items are not crafting-grid recipes and doLimitedCrafting does not reach them

badge_rule.decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'TAKE THE POWER RULE, with all 17 outlier groups applied as proposed. Every one is the rule misjudging something the data cannot see. SHELF WINS where it disagrees. Those 23 are authored. Keep all shelf badges and leave the list documented. Then switch the gate to the power rule.' The proposal is docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md
badge_rule.shelf: a TM with a counter line in data/markets.json carrying gate_badge B (stock or held_stock, price_rule income_gate) unlocks at cobblers:flag/gymB_cleared, whatever its score. This is the owner's rule, and wins over the power rule and over every outlier group below
badge_rule.unlisted: the power rule: a TM with no shelf line takes the badge an outlier group in power.outliers gives it, else the band of its score in power.scores (power.bands). Nothing else: the disc grade is a crafting price, not a badge (docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 7), and the move's type is not read

power.scores_by: tools/tm_power_score.py --server-dir <snapshot> (needs node; --check says whether the committed table is current). tools/tm_gate.py does not score: it reads the committed table and fails closed when the server's Mega Showdown moves.js has another sha256 than the one the table records, when the table lacks a TM the server crafts, or when a table row's power_badge is not its score's band

bands.rounding: the score is rounded to 0.1 first, as the table prints it; a top is inclusive
bands.why: the proposal's bands (docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 3), not retuned: badge 1 below 35; then each badge is one step of ten base power plus up to four points of side effects (badge 3 holds the 60-power moves, 5 the 80s, 6 the 90s, 7 the 100s); badge 8 above 104. The tops sit four above the round numbers because base powers cluster on them: with tops exactly on 80 and 90, Crunch and Shadow Ball (81.6) came out a badge after Dragon Claw (80), and Thunderbolt (93) a badge after Surf (90)

power.outliers_are: the 17 groups of docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 6, each applied as its 'Suggested' column says, and group 18 (Spore, the owner, 2026-10-08). `place` is a hand badge for a TM with no shelf line (a placement equal to the band holds it there, and says so); `shelf_agrees` names a shelf TM the group also speaks of, whose shelf line already is the group's badge (tools/tm_gate.py fails if the shelf moves away from it); `not_placed` names a TM the group's text mentions but its suggestion does not place, with why. A placement on a shelf TM is refused: the shelf wins

outliers.name: Thunder Wave
outliers.misjudges: valued as a Surf (90), which is the anchor working as asked; but a mid-game status move should not wait for the badge that also brings Thunderbolt. Toxic's shelf line is 5

outliers.name: Will-O-Wisp
outliers.misjudges: burn is valued at 85 x 85% (72.2, badge 4), but it halves every physical attacker for the rest of the fight; the three status inducers stay together with Toxic

outliers.name: Nuzzle
outliers.misjudges: an inconsistency in the rule: a guaranteed paralysis on a damaging move is a 100% secondary worth 30, while the status move gets 100. Nuzzle (50, badge 2) is a Thunder Wave that also deals damage

placed_2026_10_08.decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'Inferno and Zap Cannon: place them with the group whose reasoning names them. If that group is wrong for them, say which badge and why.'
placed_2026_10_08.badge: 5, the group's badge. Inferno (62.5, band 3) and Zap Cannon (72, band 4) were left at their bands because the proposal's Suggested column named Nuzzle only, though its text names both
placed_2026_10_08.why_5_is_right: each is the group's case exactly: a 100% status on a damaging move, which the rule values as a 30-point secondary instead of the status move's 100. A hit is a Will-O-Wisp (5, group 2) or a Thunder Wave (5, group 1) plus 100 or 120 power; at 50% accuracy the status lands half as often as the status move's 85-90%, which the landed damage pays back. Not 8 by the landed 120: group 9's 'biggest single hit' reasoning is for a hit that lands, and these land one time in two
placed_2026_10_08.not_measured: No Guard or Lock-On makes either certain; which species learn both the move and the ability or Lock-On is not read here

outliers.name: Trick Room
outliers.misjudges: its value is the team's: on a slow team it decides fights, on a fast one it is negative. The AI does not play around it (76, badge 5)

outliers.misjudges: the pivot's +20 puts a 70-power move level with Surf (U-turn and Volt Switch 90, badge 6; Flip Turn 80, badge 5; Parting Shot 55, badge 3). Pivoting is good in singles, but not a 90-power move's worth

outliers.misjudges: its 1.5x against a held item (97.5) and the item removal are both code, not valued (65, badge 4). Trainers here hold items

outliers.misjudges: a +2 is valued as one 70-power hit, but it multiplies every hit after it: set-up is what sweeps a gym. The rule prices one turn, not the fight. Shell Smash stays at 8, its band

outliers.misjudges: averaging over two turns halves them (64.1 and Eternabeam 68.4, badge 4), but a gate is about the biggest single hit: 150 power deletes a leader's ace and the recharge never comes

outliers.misjudges: fixed damage is strongest early: Dragon Rage's 40 HP (40, badge 2) two-shots most Pokemon at cap 25-30, and Sonic Boom (18, badge 1) the same way. The nominal values assume a level-50 user. Seismic Toss and Night Shade (65, badge 4) stay at 4, their band

outliers.misjudges: left at stated power on purpose (Hex, Venoshock 65 and Facade 70, badge 4; Acrobatics 55, badge 3; Weather Ball 50, badge 2). Each doubles in a condition a player can set up: 130, 130, 140, 110, 100

outliers.name: band edges
outliers.misjudges: a 30% side effect pushes a 90 or an 80 over the four-point allowance: Sludge Bomb (94.5, badge 7) against Psychic (90.8, 6); Iron Head (84.5, 6) against X-Scissor (80, 5). Poison Jab keeps its shelf 5

outliers.name: Return and Frustration
outliers.misjudges: nominal 100 (badge 7) assumes full (or zero) friendship; measured below: full power is cheap to reach long before badge 7, so the nominal value stands

placed_2026_10_08.decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'Return and Frustration: measure friendship speed before placing them. If it is fast, they deserve more than 6.' and 'If friendship maxes quickly, Return at full power is a 102-power hit and belongs where 102 sits on the power bands.'
placed_2026_10_08.badge: 7, the band 102 sits in (94.1-104), which is also their own score's band (100): the placement holds them there, raised from the proposal's 6
placed_2026_10_08.why: full power is reached by a purchase, not by the campaign's length. Return: a Pokemon walked out of its ball to 160 (3.7 hours out, 1.8 with a Soothe Bell, which is craftable from the start), then 8 malasadas (6 with the bell) reaches 255: Return 102 from the first badge-4 counter (greenhollow, gym4_town, 900 each; steepside in tea_town sells them at 700 with no badge on the counter). Frustration: faster still: 79 species start at 0 (Frustration 102 the moment it is taught), four of the eight starters among them (Cosmog, Type: Null, Poipole, Meltan), and every level-up only raises friendship by 2-3, so a base-0 starter at cap 25 has 60 (Frustration 78). Without items Return tops out at 80 (band 5), which is why the proposal's 6 looked safe; with them 102 is a few thousand away at badge 4, three badges before the other 100-power moves

measured.source: Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar and mega_showdown-fabric-1.0.2+1.8+1.21.1-release.jar, server-snapshot-2026-10-05, read with javap and zipfile 2026-10-08; nothing run in game
measured.power: Mega Showdown moves.js: Return = floor(happiness x 10 / 25) || 1, Frustration = floor((255 - happiness) x 10 / 25) || 1, so 102 at 255 (Return) or 0 (Frustration). Cobblemon packs the Pokemon's friendship into the Showdown team (BattleRegistry calls Pokemon.getFriendship while packing)
measured.max: config/cobblemon/main.json maxPokemonFriendship 255 (modpack and snapshot); Cobblemon has no friendship-rate multiplier in its config
measured.start: a new Pokemon takes its form's baseFriendship (Pokemon init, FormData.getBaseFriendship); the species data: 837 at 50, 79 at 0, 73 at 35, 15 at 100, 11 at 140, 5 at 90, 3 at 20, 2 at 70. A starter is no different: our eight (modpack/config/cobblemon/starters.json, level 5) start at Cosmog 0, Type: Null 0, Poipole 0, Meltan 0, Misdreavus 35, Kubfu 50, Smeargle 50, Larvesta 50. The Friend Ball sets 150 on capture (PokeBalls: CaptureEffects.friendshipSetter(150)); the Luxury Ball's FriendshipEarningBoostEffect.apply does nothing in 1.8.0
measured.start_corrected_2026_10_08: 'A starter is no different' is contradicted by the bytecode (read 2026-10-08, javap; not run in game): only a NATURAL spawn sets its form's base (PokemonSpawnAction.createEntity calls setFriendship(form.getBaseFriendship())), and a trade resets to it (TradeManager.performTrade). A starter is built by PokemonProperties.create (CobblemonStarterHandler.chooseStarter): new Pokemon() takes the base of PokemonSpecies.random()'s standard form (a random implemented species), then apply() sets the species and initialize() runs, and neither touches friendship (Pokemon has no other friendship write). So our base-0 starters (Cosmog, Type: Null, Poipole, Meltan) start at a random species' base, 50 four times in five, 0 one time in thirteen. Of the four, only Type: Null and Poipole can learn Frustration at all (legacy learnset). docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 10
measured.level_up: Pokemon.addExperienceWithPlayer, per level gained: +3 at friendship 0-99, +2 at 100-199, +0 at 200 and above (FriendshipMutationCalculator SWORD_AND_SHIELD_LEVEL_UP). Levels alone stop at 200-202: Return 80
measured.walking: PlayerPartyStore.onSecondPassed: every 120 seconds, +1 to each party Pokemon that is sent out or on a shoulder, while its friendship is below 160 (30 an hour; 50 -> 160 in 220 minutes)
measured.battle: no battle win or battle turn raises friendship: no battle class calls incrementFriendship. An X item used in battle gives +1 (XStatItem, DireHitItem, GuardSpecItem)
measured.soothe_bell: Cobblemon.preInitialize, on FriendshipUpdatedEvent: a positive change is multiplied by 1.5 (rounded) while the Pokemon holds an item tagged cobblemon:held/is_friendship_booster (the Soothe Bell only). Recipe data/cobblemon/recipe/soothe_bell.json: iron ingredients and wool, ungated
measured.items: friendship berries (Pomeg, Kelpsy, Qualot, Hondew, Grepa, Tamato; data/cobblemon/mechanics/berries.json friendshipRaiseAmount): +10 below 100, +5 below 200, +1 above: 55 berries from 200 to 255 (28 with the bell). CobbleCuisine (config/cobblecuisine.json, a config value; that it is a flat gain at every friendship is NOT read from its code): malasada +12, Poke Puff +6. Cobblemon's own cooked Poke Puff: by flavour against nature (PokePuffUtils.calculateFriendshipChange), not quantified. Bitter remedies lower it (data/cobblemon/mechanics/remedies.json: Revival Herb -15, Energy Root -10, the others -5); no counter sells them (data/markets.json)
measured.return_at_each_cap: Return's power for a base-50 starter caught at level 5 and levelled to each badge's cap (badge 1-7: caps 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55; docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 3), by level-ups alone: 42, 46, 50, 54, 58, 62, 66; holding a Soothe Bell: 52, 58, 64, 70, 76, 80, 80. Frustration for a base-0 starter, level-ups alone: 78, 72, 66, 60, 56, 52, 48. Walking and items move either to 102: Return by 8 malasadas after walking to 160 (6 with the bell), Frustration by staying at 0 (bitter remedies)

outliers.name: Spore, lowered for Stun Spore
outliers.misjudges: nothing in Spore's own score: a 100% sleep is valued 110 (band 8), and Spore is the best status move a TM teaches. The rule cannot see that Spore is also an INPUT: TMCraft's tm_stunspore recipe takes tm_spore, so the chain rule (badge_rule.chain) raised Stun Spore, a 75% paralysis at band 5, to badge 8 with it. The owner chose to lower the input rather than leave the paralysis move at 8

placed_2026_10_08.decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'STUN SPORE: lower Spore rather than leaving Stun Spore at 8. A paralysis move at badge 8 is too late; it is a mid-game tool. Spore is strong, but Stun Spore pulling it down is the right trade. Say what badge that puts Spore at, and whether it lands in the outlier group Thunder Wave sits in.'
placed_2026_10_08.badge: 5: Stun Spore's own band (score 75), so the two open together and Stun Spore needs no chain raise. Not by breaking the chain rule: the input is placed by hand here, and the chain rule then finds nothing to raise
placed_2026_10_08.why_its_own_group: not group 1 (Thunder Wave). Group 1 says a status move valued at its own band should not wait for the badge that also brings Thunderbolt; group 3 says a guaranteed status on a damaging move is undervalued. Spore is neither: the rule values it right, and it moves for a reason outside its score, the recipe that takes it. Sleep is not paralysis either: a sleeping target does not act at all for its sleep turns, where a paralysed one still acts three times in four (Showdown's 25% full paralysis), and the score table already values them apart: sleep 110, paralysis 100 (docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 2.2). Filing Spore with Thunder Wave would record a reason that is not the one the owner gave
placed_2026_10_08.what_it_costs: Spore (100% sleep) now opens at 5 with Sleep Powder and Lovely Kiss (75% sleep, band 5) and a badge before Glare (100% paralysis, group 17's 6): a guaranteed sleep before a guaranteed paralysis, which inverted the scores. Resolved 2026-10-08: the owner moved Glare to 5 (group 17), so the two open together

shelf_disagreements.why: the 21 shelf lines the power rule would place at another badge (docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md 5); Shock Wave (3) and Overheat (7) agree. Every one keeps its SHELF badge (the owner: 'Those 23 are authored. Keep all shelf badges and leave the list documented'). The shelf is laid out by gym type, so the early gyms' strong moves sell early and the late gyms' weak ones late; where the owner thinks a line is wrong, the fix is the shelf line in data/markets.json, not this list. tools/tm_gate.py fails when this list stops being exactly the disagreements (a score or a shelf line that moved), and names the line. power_badge is the score's band, before any outlier group
shelf_disagreements.outlier_means: the outlier group that also speaks of this shelf line agrees with the shelf badge (its shelf_agrees)

chain.decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'The four chain TMs opening before their source: fix it. A craft that unlocks before its input is a dead recipe.' Enforced for every TM: badge(chain TM) >= badge(its input TM)
chain.rule: after the shelf, the outlier groups and the bands, tools/tm_gate.py chain_order raises every TM whose crafting recipe takes another TM (tm_howl is tm_leer + a gem + a glove) to that input's badge, to a fixpoint. Only the chain TM moves, and only up: the input is never lowered. A shelf TM is never raised (the shelf wins): one crafted from a later TM fails the plan, for the owner to move a shelf line. Every raise is listed here, exactly, or the plan fails; then every recipe is checked again, and one that opens before its input fails the plan
chain.raises_are: item, the input TM that sets its badge, from (the badge the shelf, an outlier group or the band gave it) and to (the input's badge). Measured on the 2026-10-05 snapshot: three chains raised, one input each, no cascade; a fourth (Stun Spore from Spore) needs no raise since outlier group 18 placed Spore at Stun Spore's own badge

raises.why: Bone Club (56.5, band 3) is crafted from Bonemerang (90, band 6): it waits for Bonemerang's badge. Three badges late for a 65-power move, the cost of a recipe that needs a badge-6 TM in hand
Noble Roar (30, band 1) is crafted from Roar (45, band 2)
Triple Kick (46.8, band 2) is crafted from Double Kick (60, band 3)

superseded_raises.why: Stun Spore (75, band 5) is crafted from Spore (110, band 8, left at its band by outlier group 17): it waits for badge 8. The largest move, three badges; lowering Spore is the other fix and is not this rule's to make
superseded_raises.superseded_by: outlier group 18 (the owner, 2026-10-08: 'lower Spore rather than leaving Stun Spore at 8'): Spore at 5, so Stun Spore opens at its own band 5 and the chain rule raises nothing. Not read by tools/tm_gate.py; kept as the raise the owner overruled

chain.superseded: until 2026-10-08 a chain TM was placed by its own score and the plan only noted, 'by design', that these four opened before their input, on the reasoning that the input could come from the shelf, loot or a trade first. The owner rejected it: a recipe that opens before its input is dead for anyone who has not found the input elsewhere

badge_rule.grade_order_is: TMCraft's disc grades, lowest first: the score table's disc_grade column (the crafting price). Not a badge input

superseded_unlisted.rule: max(type_badge, grade_badge). type_badge: the lowest badge whose leader's first-win TM pool (data/progression.json first_win_rewards, the active series) holds a TM of the same gem type; a type no leader teaches (bug, flying, fighting, ghost, dragon, dark, steel, ice, fairy) takes the LAST leader's badge (8), never minimum_badge. grade_badge: the lowest shelf badge among shelf TMs whose blank disc is at least as high a grade as this TM's (grade_order). A chain TM never came before its input TM
superseded_unlisted.placed: the snapshot of 2026-10-05: 802 TMs at {1: 134, 2: 23, 3: 47, 4: 39, 5: 78, 6: 65, 7: 89, 8: 327}; the 300 TMs of the nine types no leader teaches all waited for badge 8
superseded_unlisted.superseded_by: the power rule above (the owner, 2026-10-08). Kept because it is the reasoning the owner rejected: 'gate a TM by what it does, not by its type or which leader teaches it' (docs/mechanics/TM_POWER_GATE.md, the owner's direction)

devices.items_are: fnmatch patterns on a recipe's result id. carved_wood:<wood>_crafter is Carved Wood's own crafter block (CWCrafterBlock, beside a CrafterBlockEntityAccessor mixin), made by its per-wood shaped recipes; carved_wood:oak_crafter makes a plain minecraft:crafter
devices.vanilla_why: the vanilla jar's own ids (data/minecraft/recipe/crafter.json and data/minecraft/advancement/recipes/redstone/crafter.json in 1.21.1), gated and closed even when the build cannot read a vanilla jar (Carved Wood overrides both at the same paths, so the sweep sees them through it today)
devices.badge: the highest badge any gated TM needs (computed)
devices.why: a crafting device that never asks the recipe book crafts every TM for anyone. The Crafter (vanilla 1.21.1 CrafterBlock looks the recipe up with no player) and Tom's Storage's crafting terminal (toms_storage_fabric-1.21-2.3.0.jar CraftingTerminalBlockEntity calls RecipeManager.getRecipeFor (method_8132) and nothing that reads doLimitedCrafting or the recipe book) are bypasses, read from the jars 2026-10-08. Their own crafting recipes are gated like a TM, at the last TM badge. Carved Wood's carved_wood:wooden_crafter is a SPECIAL recipe (CrafterRecipe extends class_1852, CustomRecipe: isSpecial, so doLimitedCrafting never applies) that makes a minecraft:crafter from mixed crafting tables; it is closed, and the per-wood shaped crafter recipes still make one. Sophisticated Core's crafting upgrade calls method_7665 and obeys the gamerule
devices.owner_review: this withholds the Crafter and the crafting terminal until the last TM badge, for every player. Set enforced false to give them back and accept that either one crafts any TM
devices.owner_decision: the owner, 2026-10-08: 'DEVICES: keep them gated at badge 8.' enforced stays true

regivers.found: COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31.zip data/cobbleverse/function/starter_pack.mcfunction runs `recipe give @s *`; it is the reward of data/cobblemon/advancement/root.json in the same pack, whose one criterion is {"trigger": "cobblemon:pick_starter"} (read 2026-10-08). So every player who picked a starter already holds every recipe, TMs included, and a player who picks one after the gate synced them would get every TM back
regivers.answer: an advancement of ours on the same trigger, cobblers:tm_gate/resync/<n>, resets the player's cobblers.tmgate score and revokes itself: the next tick re-syncs them after the starter pack has run, whichever reward ran first

does_not_cover: Cobblemon 1.8's own TM Machine (cobblemon:tm_machine) prints native TMs from data/cobblemon/tms/*.json (335 moves: 128 cobblemon:default, always offered; 206 cobblemon:unlockable; 1 cobblemon:advancement), from gems: Earthquake is 10 ground gems, soft sand and a diamond. It is a block-entity menu, not the recipe book, so this gate does not touch it. Read from the jar 2026-10-08: ObtainMethod.matches (PlayerHasAdvancementObtainMethod's per-player check) has no caller in Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar, and only the client's TechnicalMachine.filterTms filters the list. Decided, the owner, 2026-10-08: 'THE TM MACHINE: leave it ungated and accept it as the gem route.' It stays ungated: a player with the gems can print a native TM of any default move before its badge, by design
a crafted TM is an item: a player who holds the badge can craft one and hand it to a player who does not
a TM from loot, a trade or a counter is not a crafted TM; the shelf has its own gate (its price)
TMCraft's Move Tutor Table and Pokemon Breeder Table, and its tutor_* and egg_* items, are code, not recipes: not read
a world that had the pack removed keeps doLimitedCrafting true (a gamerule is saved with the world): run cobblers:tm_gate/off first. Every player keeps the recipes the last sync gave
a recipe a mod adds at runtime in code rather than as a data file is not in the sweep; `recipe give @s *` still gives it, so it is never stranded, only uncounted

the world's own datapacks folder is not read by the sweep (no world is read): a world-local pack's recipes are given by `recipe give @s *` but not counted, and a world-local pack's TM recipe would not be gated
